verified_limits: The Marquis is murdered the night of his return, not months later; the brother shelters the youngest sister before confrontation.
Old-regime harm is not erased or treated as historically interchangeable with revolutionary violence. Victim suffering does not authorize killing an innocent child.
Lucie and child have already escaped when Pross stays behind; protection is concrete, not historical absolution.
Darnay does not consent to the substitution; loving intent does not automatically justify coercive means. Helpers risk harm and loved ones grieve.
Physical resemblance remains essential, while the classification critique is an interpretation rather than its replacement.
The text does not promise that denunciation would save the seamstress or invent a forgone life-saving bargain.
The ending remains the narrator’s conditional imagined speech, not documented last words or a rule validating disappointed lives through useful death.
conclusion: Full review completed after the recorded corrections. No unresolved substantive mismatch identified.
limits: AI editorial review, not human native-speaker certification.
Uses the checked Chinese/English and correction record; does not claim a new full reading of Dickens’s novel or independent verification of every factual correction.
Foreign renditions reorganize Chinese short rhetorical paragraphs into developed prose, not sentence-by-sentence translations.
